## 1. What must precede what, with the anchor for each constraint

### (a) #33 has two hard predecessors, and both are still owed

> **§92.3** — "**LG-9..12 still wait on POP-1 itself**, now with C-POPF-2 as their exact consumption seam; POP-1 lands the TIER_POP refusal pin instead of the phantom."

> **§49** (the §46c correction) — "REFUTED — there IS no caravan reception machinery at HEAD; migration landing is unconditional with no capacity read (demographicsMigration.js:453-482). POP-1's arrival clearing would be the FIRST refusal machinery in the tree, so **§46c's cover mechanics are BLOCKED-ON POP-1**, not consumers of it. **Sequencing recorded: POP-1 precedes the §46c spy waves.**"

> **§99.3** — "⚠ The Q10 **BAND-WALKER PREFIX** is confirmed STILL OWED (it rode neither eff train) — **it must land before any LG band**; docketed to the next infra member."

Slot check: `src/domain/worldPulse/demographicsMigration.js` exists; searched `receptionContract`, `arrivalClearing`, `caravanIntake`, `refusalBySuspicion` — **0 hits**, so POP-1's reception contract is still unbuilt. No `band-walker` prefix instrument found under `tests/lint` (the three `*Band*.walker.test.js` files are `spBandFamilies`, `lawBandTable`, `habitBandsReconciliation` — none is the Q10 prefix). **Both predecessors stand.**

So: **POP-1 → #33's cover members; the Q10 band-walker prefix → any #33 band.** POP-1 is a member of #32 (the POP family). **#32 therefore partially precedes #33** — not as a whole, but on this one spine.

### (b) #33 also carries an unanswered owner question that blocks its design, not its build

> Brief #33: "One directive inside it — **whether wartime military use preempts trade use of limited capacity** — was asked of you and never answered." (ODQ **§125.1**.)

The unified vessel pool is *one* machinery with two modes (**§46a** chair note: "this replaces the committed-for-the-duration sketch with a UNIFIED VESSEL-POOL model (one machinery, two modes)"). Preemption is the allocation rule at the centre of that pool, so it is **architecture-blocking**, not a late tuning value. It must be on the sitting **before** #33's design lane, not before its build lane.

### (c) #18 is gated on the banked rewrite; the others are not

> Brief #18 — "*Depends on:* **the banked prose rewrite's desks and its §920 landing**."

This is the only one of the six with that dependency. See §3 below.

### (d) #20 is last of the build acts, by two independent anchors

> **§482.2** (via brief #20) — "**ONE trailing OSR mint**", run "after the very last content car, so that the whole run costs one mint rather than many."

> **§739.2** — "THE LAUNCH BUILD AFTER THIS RULING: … catalog residue incl. DEITY-LIVE-CHECK + graveyard · **ONE OSR mint · parity (re-scoped) → ultra [OWNER] → walk + ONE regen → terminal soak → tuning [OWNER] → push [OWNER]**."

And #20's own two extra rungs are **consequences** of what lands before it, not independent work: "two further schema rungs are already spoken for by an exemption that was declared retired and never was, and by twenty-five keys that become visible the moment the default preset lights" (§900/§902). **Anything that widens a persisted shape — #32's persisted-field batch, #33's "declared widening of saved data", the encounters keys — lands before #20 or forces a second mint.** That is the whole economic point of the item.

### (e) The freeze wall, and what it actually fences

> **§764.3** — "TE-TRANS-1 (arch→panel→build; **the LAST same-seed-moving wave**) → TE-GOLDEN-1 (freezes the WIDENED corpus at the post-TRANS bytes) → residue → OSR mint → parity → [ULTRA, owner keystroke] → walk + ONE regen → TERMINAL SOAK… Sequencing law inside the amendment: **TRANS before GOLDEN** (never freeze a corpus you are about to move), both before the soak."

> **§881.4** (owner, verbatim: *"oh light everything up before the exhaustive review."*) — "the arc is now TAIL-F → T13 (+ mint riders) → HORIZON-INSTR → HORIZON-DARK → **LIGHTING WAVE** → GOLDEN freeze (records the LIT world, so no per-flag door signature is owed) → W-ARMS → walk + ONE regen → **the exhaustive review (§879.6)** → the terminal soak → the tuning signature (VALUES only, still LAST) → push."

⛔ **§764.3's sentence is under live amendment.** `docs/OWNER_SITTING_2026-09-15.md` item 1 puts it to the owner by name, with the chair's default: *"AMEND §764.3 to 'TRANS was the last same-seed-moving wave BEFORE the long tail; the tail's output-moving cars land as one declared shift before TE-GOLDEN-1, each priced by name'"* — because five measured hygiene cars already contradict it (§928.4). **The freeze register is still `frozenAt` null**, so the wall is a *sentence*, not yet a mechanism. Every ordering claim below that leans on the freeze is therefore sound; the items' *legality* under the sentence is item 1's to settle.

### (f) #21 comes after the walk, not before it — and the brief has this backwards

> **§879.6** (owner, verbatim clauses 4–5) — "(4) *'We will be doing a full systematic comprehension, exhaustive review analysis and fix **right before the soak**'*; (5) *'so my goal right now is just to finish building and landing everything **then we do a review**'*." Chair ruling in the same row: "**the exhaustive review+fix is a chartered PHASE after the last landing and before the soak** — its slot relative to the GOLDEN freeze is ruled when the last car lands (a fix that can move an output lands before the freeze or rides its governed door; vetoable)."

**§881.4 settled that open slot**: freeze → W-ARMS → walk + ONE regen → **then** the review. Every handoff pickup since has repeated it in the same words — "the owner's WALK + one regen → the exhaustive review → fix cars → **FULL STOP before the terminal soak**" (`docs/HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:142`, `:153`, `:169`, `:181`, and the §894/§891 pickups at `:236`, `:285`).

⚠ **The brief's own ordering (#21 → #22 → #23) contradicts this** and is the stale spelling. The brief's #22 also carries a dead dependency: it says the billed keystroke was "re-sequenced to run after the dwellings work so that the review covers it" (§464.4/§482.2) — but **§739.1 moved the DW programme to the post-launch module by owner order** ("THE DW PROGRAM (~42 cars) → MODULE (owner order by name)"). That re-sequencing reason no longer exists; #22's position is now free and should be re-ruled rather than inherited.

### (g) The realm/settlement boundary — #34 survives it, and this is worth quoting because it is the one that gets lanes wrong

> **§738.1** (owner, in-chat) — *"anything involving settlement layer mapmaking is deferred until after launch and is part of the module."* … "⛔ **THE DISTINCTION EVERY LANE MUST HOLD:** the **REALM/WORLD map** (the FMG-fork surface, `src/components/map/**`, `public/map/**`, the spatial digest/capture, realm plates) is **LAUNCH-CORE** — the WEAVE cars that carry map words (CAP capture/banding · NET roads/sea drawing · POLIS overlays/territory/travel rings · VAR heightmap DSL · SEAM bridge repairs) are ALL realm-side by charter and stay. The **SETTLEMENT map** … is MODULE-SIDE, post-launch."

So today's owner ruling (#32/#33/#34 launch-path) is **consistent** with §738, not a reversal of it. No re-ask is owed.

### (h) Landing ≠ sealing — the gate that catches an over-eager #32

> **START_HERE.md:469** — "⛔ **LANDING IS NOT SEALING.** EP is a DRAFT AT ROUND SEVEN; HB's round four has NO RECORDED CLOSE; WC is ARCHITECTED, NOT STARTED. **Owner gates still standing: CR-WC-9 (WC's persisted field batch), WY F9 `supplyCargo` UNSIGNED (WC-10 hard-gates on it), EP's four §7a parked rows, HB Q1's two persisted fields.**"

Slot check: `supplyCargo` → **0 hits in `src` and `tests`**. The gate is real and unbuilt. These are **three of the four gates the brief names inside #32** — and they are already on the owner's sitting as item 16, "The persisted-shape rulings". #32 can run to the gate but not through it.

## 2. Which of these move output, and which do not

The distinction that matters is **not** "engine vs UI" — it is **dark vs lit**. A flag-gated wave landing dark is byte-identical by construction, and the estate enforces it: `tests/property/` carries ~30 `*DormancyFence`/`*DormancyGolden` suites (`chanceEncountersDormancyFence.test.js`, `espionageDormancyFence.test.js`, `casusCommerciiDormancyFence.test.js`, …), and `simulationRules.js:238` names the cell they close — "the flag-dark/value-present cell, which is the one cell dark byte-identity has to close."

The precedent is explicit: **§881.13(4)** placed the encounters train *after* T13, the last same-seed-moving wave — "the train lands **DARK** on its own gate after T13 …, **golden 0/525 and fences at both arms**, and LIGHTS in the lighting wave as a declared shift with every other door — the freeze records it lit." A dark landing after the mover-wall is lawful.

| Item | Output-moving? | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **#32** engine family waves | **NO at landing, YES at lighting.** Each wave lands behind its own `*Enabled` key with a dormancy fence proving 0 movement. | The flag-mint law itself (§49.3, §50.2: every flag-minting packet carries the subsystemRows path, the seven edge-shared bundles, and the literal flag drive). Its output moves in the lighting wave / ONE REGEN, as a **declared** shift. |
| **#33** logistics & vessels | **NO at landing.** Brief: "It carries **two flags, dark by construction**, and a declared widening of saved data." | Same architecture. ⚠ But the **saved-data widening is not output; it is schema**, and that binds it to #20, not to the freeze. |
| **#34** — the built remainder | **N/A** — already landed, under their own flags (`treasuryEnabled`, `foreignSeatEnabled`, `interventionEnabled`, `irregularForceEnabled`, `legitimacyUpheavalEnabled`, `settlementPoliticsEnabled`). | Verified at `simulationRules.js`. |
| **#34** — W-ARMS | **NO if flag-gated, YES otherwise.** §881.15's re-cut arc deliberately puts it *after* the freeze: "→ the GOLDEN freeze as ONE landing carrying COVERAGE Cars 1–4 → **W-ARMS with nothing of HORIZON's**." A post-freeze slot is only survivable dark. | ⚠ **Flag it or move it.** A generative heraldry programme that writes reader-visible arms into a dossier is output-moving by nature; the post-freeze placement is a bet on a dark landing that nothing has yet proved. Price it before boarding. |
| **#18** display trains | **SPLIT — and this is the trap.** Layout/affordance cars do not move output (§826: "VAR-3 knob pins … a **DECLARED UI shift; generation untouched**"). Cars that change **composed sentences** do. | §930.6 shows both halves in one week: LT38's landing ladder is non-moving; LT41's cars 4–5 (eleven conflict sentences, five origin dashes) are "HELD as OUTPUT-MOVING under §764.3". **Classify #18 car by car, never train by train.** |
| **#20** the OSR mint + parity | **NO.** An instrument/register act. The slot's own HEAD says it: `f73bdbf16` — "rung 18 still; **no OSR movement at this landing**." | It is the *consumer* of schema movement, never a producer of output. |
| **#21** the exhaustive review | **ITS FIXES CAN BE.** §879.6: "a fix that can move an output lands before the freeze **or rides its governed door**." | This is the live tension. See below. |

### The consequence the owner's new ruling creates

Moving #32/#33/#34 ahead of #21 is **the cheap direction** under the same-seed law — precisely because those three land dark, and a dark landing costs the freeze nothing. The expensive direction was already there and is untouched: **#21's fixes.** With the review sitting after the freeze (§881.4), every output-moving fix it finds must ride a **governed door**, and the estate has exactly one door-minting law:

> `docs/HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:366` — "A landed fence (`espionageDormancyFence.test.js:332`) re-records the driven-corpus constant **ONLY inside a NAMED CHARTERED WINDOW**, and *'exactly ONE remains: the LIGHTING WAVE (§881.4)'*."

**That window is spent** — the lighting wave landed at §898–§906. So today there is **no open door** for an output-moving fix found by #21. Either the sitting's item 1 amendment opens one, or #21's output-moving findings have nowhere to land. **This is the single highest-value thing to put in front of the owner alongside the #32/#33/#34 ruling**, and it is not currently on the sitting.

## 3. Is the banked prose rewrite a dependency of any of them?

**Yes — of #18 alone. No — of #32, #33, #34, #20 or #21.**

The brief states it directly for #18: "*Depends on:* **the banked prose rewrite's desks and its §920 landing**." No other item's `Depends on:` line names it.

Slot-verified state of the rewrite (CONFIRMED by `git merge-base --is-ancestor`):

- **Wave 8a is LANDED on the slot.** `f4005cccd` (8a-1, "the index-stable draw lands") through `cea20ddb3` (8a-13) are all ancestors of `f73bdbf16`.
- **Everything after it is banked off-slot.** `7992713d0` (the DS-DEF-2 batch-4 dock), `d610e371d` (8b DS-DEF-2 cure v3), `dc5facadd` / `94a6f33f4` (the CLARITY batches), `600771812` (`lane-scribe`) — **none is an ancestor of the slot.**

So the rewrite is **PART-LANDED**, and the banked half is what #18 waits on. Owner's word, `docs/HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:27`, ~17:2x on 09-14: *"bank the prose rewrite and go straight to the rest long tail chain"* — nothing resumes without him.

⛔ **The Scribe lineage cannot be used as a back door.** Memory, §930.9: `lane-scribe` `600771812` "descends from the BANKED rewrite dock (`7992713d0`… is its ancestor; **57 of its 107 cars are REWRITE cars, four of them DECLARED simulation shifts**)… it lands only when the rewrite lands, on the owner's word."

**Therefore #18 is not schedulable today**, and today's ruling does not unblock it. #32/#33/#34 are genuinely independent of the bank — which is exactly why they are the right work to take up the slots #18 cannot use.

---

## 4. Proposed lane order

Four lanes maximum (FOLD 57's cap; research exempt). Owner-gated classes are marked and are not started by any lane.

Output: a real remaining-wave roster with POP-1's position in it. | Everything downstream needs a number that is not 5½ weeks old, and §3j forbids restating the old one. This is hours, not days, and it retires the only UNKNOWN in this read. |
| **1** | **POP-1 + the Q10 band-walker prefix** (one lane, two cars) | The **only hard blocker among the six**, and it blocks the item with the longest build (#33) by two independent anchors (§92.3, §99.3). Correcting that costs one lane and changes the owner's picture of the whole tail. Land it here rather than at §881.15's post-freeze slot: **its dark-landing claim is unproved**, and proving it before the freeze is free while proving it after is not. |

It stops cleanly at CR-WC-9 / WY F9 `supplyCargo` / HB Q1 — all three already on the sitting as item 16, so the stop is a report, not a stall. **Landing dark, so it is free under the same-seed law** in either reading of §764.3. |
| **4** | **#33 — design first, build second** | Boards only when lane 1 lands. Its **design** needs §125.1's preemption answer (allocation is the centre of a unified pool, §46a), so put that question on the sitting **now**, during lanes 0–3, not when the build lane is idle waiting for it. Charter must name `blockadeTransport.js:20`'s `/airship/i` institution-name regex as a collision surface. |

That is read-only, costs one cheap lane, and is the difference between #18 landing in one window and thrashing across three. |
| **6** | **#20** — the single trailing mint, **after the last schema-bearing car of 1–5** | By construction (§482.2: "ONE trailing OSR mint"; §739.2 puts it immediately before ultra/walk). It must swallow #33's declared saved-data widening and #32's persisted batch in the same act, or the estate pays two mints for one run. Currently at rung 18 (`.observed-shape-readers-baseline.json`), with rungs 19–20 already spoken for. |
| **7** | **GOLDEN freeze** — ⛔ **OWNER**, and **only after the sitting's item 1 is initialled** | "Nobody freezes a corpus they are about to move" (§764.3). The register is `frozenAt` null today, so nothing is broken yet — but the freeze cannot be signed while the amendment that governs what may still move is un-initialled. |
| **8** | **Walk + ONE regen** — ⛔ **OWNER** | §881.4, §3h step 4–5. ⚠ Standing blocker, unrelated to this read: brief #23 records "the review corpus currently contains no settlement with a patron, so faith cannot be judged on the walk until that roster widens" (and `HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:181`: "NOT READY: deity-free corpus 0/44"). |

### The two things to put to the owner now

1. **The governed door for #21's output-moving fixes.** The one named window (the lighting wave) is spent; §879.6 promised a door and none is open. Without it, the review can find an output-moving defect and have nowhere to land the cure. Ruling this costs the owner one line and is the difference between a review that can fix things and a review that can only file them. **Not currently on the sitting.**
2. **W-ARMS's true size, and its slot.** The sitting is carrying #34 as an XL cluster "mostly stopped on a single owner row apiece". Four of its five members are landed; the fifth is W-ARMS, and W-ARMS's own owner rows are Car 0's six owed measurements (§879.11 R2, §880.5), not a design question. Correcting the record here is cheap and it shrinks the tail visibly.

### Deferred and written down, not dropped

- **#18's six trains** — deferred on the banked rewrite, on the owner's own word of 09-14 ~17:2x. *Deliberately deferred — documented, not a bug to re-find.* Its car-classification pass is scheduled above so the deferral costs nothing when it lifts.
- **#22's position** — its recorded reason ("after the dwellings work so that the review covers it") died with §739.1's module descope. Flagged for re-ruling; not re-sequenced by this read, because the brief's §464.4/§482.2 anchor is the owner's and only he can retire it.
- **The brief's #21-before-#23 ordering** — refuted above against §881.4 and six handoff pickups. Recorded here rather than silently corrected in the brief, which is not mine to edit.

**Labels:** every build-state verdict in §0 and §1 is **CONFIRMED** (executed greps and `git merge-base` against the slot at `f73bdbf16`, paths and lines quoted). The #32 remaining-wave count is **UNKNOWN** with its reason. The claim that W-ARMS is output-moving-unless-flagged is **PLAUSIBLE** — reasoned from the nature of a generative programme, not measured; lane 2's Car 0 measures it.

result.summary:
Item #34 bundles seven designed programmes. The brief says they "stand sealed and unbuilt"; the RECORD says that is true of exactly two of them and stale for the other five — this is the §928/§930 pattern again, the record corrected by later record.
W-COIN: the "two questions you have not answered" are Q10 and Q11 (§737.1). Both were RULED by the chair at §763.2 under the owner's omnibus grant, and the treasury LANDED — W-COIN-1a/1b at §793 (CAS 14707a8a8), W-COIN-2/3/4 as T2·COIN at §842 (CAS acaaad63f), "coffers, upkeep, shortfalls, the conservation walker, coin news".
W-SEAT: not "queued" — SEAT-1 (§823), SEAT-2c/3/4 (§844, landed §861), SEAT-2b+SEAT-5 (§870.4, landed in the §876 WAR-TRUTH consist), SEAT-7a (the SEAT-78 dock, 3 cars, landed in the §900 desk consist). SEAT-6 is deferred-priced; SEAT-8 is the open half.
The WEAVE: largely landed — NAME-1/3/4 (§761), CAP-1..4 (§758), SEAM-3 + POLIS-1/2 + ST-3 + VAR-1a (§794), NET cars (§811/§848), ST-2 (§754). Genuinely unbuilt by the record: NAME-2, NET-2, POLIS-3/4/5, VAR-1b/2/3, ST-4, SEAM-4/5 disposition.
Encounters: the season cap that "locks out the whole world" was CURED at §893.2 (`19126aaac`, the flag-ON lit test); ENC-1..4, 4b/4c and 6 all landed §888–§900. What remains is the drift door, two never-chair-ruled persisted-shape rows (4 and 9), the tie-break row, and the tuning signature.
Genuinely sealed-and-unbuilt: W-DESK (nothing in the record after §730.3, though DESIGN_W_MEM.md:566 hints T11 built DESK-1's columns) and W-ARMS (design volume only — §896.2 landed it docs-only; Car 0's probes ran read-only; no product car).
The two operations cars are W-OPS O1 and O2 (§803 seats cars 1–7): O1 landed inside the §874 coupling; O2 was "COMPLETE AND HOLDING" at `a1981ab96` (§872.1) with a named wiring-reconcile debt.
What stops the rest: W-ARMS's one-word veto and its eleven taste rows plus the paid-rights floor; W-DESK has no owner row at all — it simply never got a slot after STRIP-6.

result.summary:
Item #33 is the chartered LG volume (ODQ §46/§46a/§46b/§46c/§125). As a VOLUME it is unbuilt: zero LG identifiers exist at the build slot (searched `L-LG-`, `LG-1|LG-5|LG-9`, `logisticsEnabled|logisticsNetwork|logisticsLayer`, `§46`, `§125` across src, tests and supabase — all zero).
But the record's headline "never been built" is WRONG on two members, and the code wins. (1) THE CIRCLE NETWORK IS BUILT AND LIVE under a different lineage — `src/domain/spatial/teleportEdges.js` (Phase 5.5 mover wave M9c, "TELEPORT BLOCS") builds a frozen clique of circle-holders with cost and capacity, it is lit in the live canonize path (`src/store/campaignSpatialCanonize.js:124` `teleport: true`), its edges fold into the routing graph, it carries a hi-fi zero-hop news lane, and it has 449 lines of tests. (2) A SUBSTANTIAL SEA-VESSEL LAYER IS BUILT AND LIT — W-NAVY (`navalLayer.js` 620 lines + `navalKernel.js` 552) with derived navies, convoys, lane capacity, sea battles and shared fate, behind `navalEnabled`, which is LIT in the three world-alive presets and the lit default.
What stops the rest: airships do not exist as a mode at all — the reserved digest slot `airField` is hard-coded null and pinned null by six tests; there is NO vessel pool in any form (zero hits for vesselPool/shipPool/vesselCount, and naval capacity is per-sea-lane, not per-settlement); NO rebuild or unavailability timer (zero hits, including the chair's own named spelling `cooldownUntil`, which exists only for the npc ladder and demographics plans); and NEITHER of the two LG flags exists — `FLAG_DEFAULTS` holds 30 keys, none circle/airship/logistics, and the virtual WAVES gate list names none either. Cargo asymmetry, rescue exceptions, envoy vessels, caravan cover, army confiscation, siege lockdown, roaming captivity and the §125.4 size-scaled speed law are all zero-hit. The declared saved-data widening never landed for LG (zero of 200 supabase migrations); the only widening that did land is the sea side's own `spatialLedgers.navalTransit`.
One record-side blocker is also CURED by the code: §49's §46c correction says caravan/group reception does not exist and "migration landing is unconditional with no capacity read" — at the slot `demographicsMigration.js` now carries a closed refusal vocabulary and capacity-ranked placement.

The envoy family itself is large and ROAD-BOUND: ~33 modules under src/domain/worldPulse (envoyErrand.js, envoyErrandTransit.js, envoyEncounter.js, envoyInterceptionStage.js, envoyRansomStage.js, namedPersonTransit.js …), and a grep of envoyErrandTransit.js and namedPersonTransit.js for teleport|sea|ship|vessel|airship|port finds no modality at all — legs are projected onto "a caller-owned frozen route" (namedPersonTransit.js:152-154 "Roads stores the whole outbound ..."). Envoy captivity DOES exist (the WR-7b foreign-guest hold, described at src/lib/spatialUsage.js:369) but is gated dark: src/domain/worldPulse/simulationRules.js:920 `envoyDiplomacyEnabled: false`, and spatialUsage.js:369 records "envoyDiplomacyEnabled is a virtual flag lit in no preset". None of it rides a vessel.

rows.name: Caravan cover for spies — group-fate coupling, population/scarcity scale factors, the individual suspicion refusal, the infiltration network channel
rows.family: LG × ES × POP (ODQ §46b item 3, §46c and its five addenda)
rows.recordSays: An entry-route spectrum: conventional approach < caravan cover (fate-coupled to the group, scaling with group size and the destination's need) < riding the target's own network (much lower odds, knowledge-gated); plus an individual-level refusal out of suspicion and rumour, and the wartime gate relaxation.
rows.evidence: Searched `caravanCover`, `coverFate`, `inheritCaravan`, `groupCover`, `entryChance`, `gateSuspicion`, `knownNetwork`, `networkKnowledge` — all zero. The espionage directory (src/domain/worldPulse/espionage/, 17 modules) holds an infiltration LADDER, which is depth-of-placement, not entry route: infiltrationDepth.js:2-5 "THE TWO NEW RUNGS (W-OPS car O3): The L3 PLACED and L4 SEATED rungs", :95 INFILTRATION_LEVELS, door at espionageGate.js:112-116 `rules.infiltrationDepthEnabled === true`. No reachability gate, no knowledge predicate, no chance multiplier tied to a caravan. NOTE — THE RECORD'S NAMED BLOCKER IS CURED BY THE CODE: ODQ §49's §46c correction says "there IS no caravan reception machinery at HEAD; migration landing is unconditional with no capacity read (demographicsMigration.js:453-482)". At the slot that is now false: src/domain/worldPulse/demographicsMigration.js:107-109 `export const MIGRATION_REFUSALS = Object.freeze(['none','partial','unreachable','no_capacity','unattractive'])`, with capacity-ranked placement and a named refusal at :232-242. The group-reception substrate §46c needed exists; the individual suspicion/rumour arm does not (searched suspicion|rumour-refusal in demographicsMigration.js and migrationKernel.js — zero).

rows.name: Confiscation — an army on the route takes a caravan, replenishes from it, or turns it back; the inspection split (observed cargo × believed destination)
rows.recordSays: An opposing army sharing a route with a caravan bound for an enemy settlement likely confiscates it — the caravan is consumed or turns back, the army acts on its BELIEF, the confiscated cargo replenishes army supply, and inspection converts cargo to observed fact while destination stays belief.
rows.evidence: Searched `confiscateCaravan`, `caravanSeizure`, `takeCargo`, `cargoInspect`, `inspectCaravan` — zero hits. Three adjacent landed families, none of which is this: (1) GATE-policy confiscation of goods at a destination, not an army on the route — src/domain/spatial/smuggle.js:250-260 "smuggle roll → (if detected ∧ hostile) SEIZURE → (elif contraband) CONFISCATION → else TOLL"; (2) caravan interception by a hostile GATE SETTLEMENT on the path — src/domain/spatial/supplyShipments.js:40-41 "INTERCEPTION (basic, v1). A gate on the route that is HOSTILE TO THE DESTINATION CUTS the shipment (`routeIntercepted`)", :209, :255; (3) supply-web warfare against supplier VILLAGES — src/domain/worldPulse/supplyWebWarfare.js:24 "THE INSTRUMENTS (§4) are one doctrine ...: raid, occupy, embargo, toll war, purchase denial, interdiction". No army-versus-caravan encounter, no turn-back reroute, no supply gain booked from a taken caravan, and no two-register observed/believed read at a checkpoint.

rows.name: Siege lockdown — a spy inside a besieged settlement cannot leave except by smuggler, tunnel, or the settlement's own circle; and capture resolution by the captor's relation
rows.family: LG (ODQ §46c third addendum item 4, fourth addendum item 1)
rows.recordSays: A spy inside a besieged settlement cannot leave except by smugglers, tunnels or transport the settlement already uses; a captured spy/envoy resolves by the captor's relation — friendly attackers release, enemy attackers hold for ransom.
rows.evidence: Searched `siegeLockdown`, `besieged.*leave`, `cannotLeave`, `exitBesieged` — 1 hit, unrelated (src/domain/worldPulse/deploymentReturn.js:521, a failed relief summary). Grep of all 17 espionage modules for siege|besieg|exfil|extract: a siege appears only as an urgency term in the mission chooser (src/domain/worldPulse/espionage/espionageMath.js:438 "URGENCY FORCES `act_now`. A siege at the gate ..."; espionageRider.js:124), and `extraction` is a hold-exit kind in infiltrationDrift.js:685-691 with no siege condition. No exit-mode set, no smuggler/tunnel channel, no captor-relation branch.

rows.name: Roaming captivity without ransom — a settlement-less NPC taken by bandits, held a bounded time, released with no ransom
rows.recordSays: An NPC roaming settlement-less may still be captured, held an appropriate time, then released with no ransom issued; may mint the first bandit-class encounter producer for settlement-less NPCs.
rows.evidence: Searched `roam`, `settlement-less`, `wanderer`, `captiv`, `bandit`. `roaming` in src/domain means the roaming STRESSOR twin, not people — src/domain/crisisLifecycle.js:7,96,101,228,532. The ransom machinery structurally requires a settlement debtor: src/domain/worldPulse/ransomClaim.js:178-184 `export function mintRansomClaim({ hold, tick, homeId, worthBand } = {})` … `const debtorId = strictText(homeId)` — so there is no no-ransom captivity arm to fall back to. `bandit` exists only as a label or flavour: src/domain/worldPulse/npcAgency.js:49 labels list, roadsKernel.js:588-589 ("a bandit road (T3) can still take an embassy that no army meets"), religionLegitimacy.js:141. No bandit-class producer for a settlement-less NPC, no time-bounded hold-then-release.

rows.name: Size-scaled travel speed for armies and migrating population columns
rows.family: LG-adjacent (ODQ §125.4; the brief routes it WY/POP-adjacent)
rows.recordSays: Armies, as organized units, travel slower than other units, scaling with size — and the same for migrating populations; the existing transit kernels gain the scaling read.
rows.evidence: The army speed law is a FLAT constant with a readiness term only: src/domain/spatial/armyTransit.js:53-57 "ARMY SPEED. An army marches SLOWER than a courier/caravan ... weeks = ceil(hopWeeks × ARMY_SPEED_FACTOR / speedMult(readiness))", `ARMY_SPEED_FACTOR: 1.5`; armyMarchWeeks :293-299 takes `(baseHopWeeks, readiness01)` and no strength or headcount. Searched `slower|speed.*size|size.*speed|columnSpeed` in armyTransit.js and src/domain/spatial/migration.js — no size read in either. The convoy twin is likewise flat (navalLayer.js:80-81 CONVOY_SPEED_FACTOR 1.2 + readiness gain).

rows.name: The two flags (circles / airships), dark by construction with dormancy byte-identity
rows.family: LG constitution (ODQ §46 chair disposition; §49.3 the flag-mint seventh-path law)
rows.recordSays: The family carries two flags — circles and airships — dark by construction, with dormancy byte-identity.
rows.evidence: NEITHER FLAG EXISTS. The UI registry is the full list and holds 30 keys, none of them LG: src/lib/flagRegistry.js:31-128 `export const FLAG_DEFAULTS = Object.freeze({ discordOauth … welcomeJourneyFilm })` — searched it for circle/airship/teleport/vessel/logistics/lg, zero. The engine-gate (virtual simulation-rules) list likewise: src/domain/worldPulse/simulationRules.js:644-654 `const WAVES = Object.freeze({ momentumEnabled, navalEnabled, interventionEnabled, settlementLifecycleEnabled, peaceEngineEnabled, supplyWebWarfareEnabled, upswingArcsEnabled, resourceDynamicsEnabled, constructiveFlowsEnabled })`. WHAT DOES EXIST is a different family's flag, and it is LIT not dark: `navalEnabled: true` at simulationRules.js:646, inside WAVES, which the header at :630-632 says are "lit TOGETHER in the three world-alive presets AND, since L-DEFAULT hunk 1, in the lit default beneath them". rows.name: The declared widening of saved data (circle / port as persisted settlement features)
rows.family: LG constitution (ODQ §46 chair disposition: "Persisted-shape widening ... is declared for the veto surface")
rows.recordSays: A declared widening of saved data rides the family and is on the owner's veto surface.

No settlement-schema field either: grep of src/domain/settlement.schema.js for teleport|airship|vessel|fleet|circle returns nothing — circles and airship docks are ordinary INSTITUTION ROSTER rows (matched by name/catalogId at teleportEdges.js:136-152). Dormant (no opt-in / <2 circle-holders) ⇒ slot null ⇒ byte-identical." ONE widening DID land, on the sea side only: navalLayer.js:12-15 "All naval state lives in a new `spatialLedgers.navalTransit` ledger (the armyTransit pattern — drop-when-empty, zero eager, no digest version-axis event)."

rows.name: Settlement-derived reinforcement and supply volume, regardless of path (ground, sea, air, or circle)
rows.family: LG (the §46 addendum, owner ~12:55: CAPACITY vs THROUGHPUT as two distinct typed reads)
rows.recordSays: How much a settlement can send reflects its tier, population and economics regardless of the path travelled; capacity (settlement-derived) and throughput (route/mode-bound) must be two distinct typed reads so neither impersonates the other.
rows.evidence: THE CAPACITY HALF EXISTS for the ground path: src/domain/worldPulse/reinforcement.js:1-10 "the REINFORCEMENT FLOW (pure) ... computed here as a pure, deterministic function of the origin's population / economic capacity / military supply chains (materiel) / food / trade / war-posture / legitimacy / manpower, the DISTANCE & route security to the front, and whether the origin is ITSELF threatened", with BASE_FLOW_FRACTION 0.06 and MAX_FLOW_FRACTION 0.10 at :35-36 and a bounded drain on the origin (:17-20). THE THROUGHPUT HALF IS NOT SEPARATED: there is no mode-bound carrying bound anywhere — the only capacity in the estate is per-sea-lane convoy slots (navalLayer.js:332) and the recorded-but-unread teleport edge capacity (teleportEdges.js:40-44 "v1 routing reads COST, not capacity (no throttle yet)"), and neither is consulted by reinforcement.js, which imports no spatial capacity read at all.

ownerQuestions.question: The ruin-filter roster walker carries a standing owner deferral over the very module that feeds the circle and port edge sets — whether a ruined or fallen settlement drops out of the teleport bloc / port set, or whether a siege only starves the node.
ownerQuestions.source: tests/lint/ruinFilterRoster.walker.test.js:188 — `'src/domain/spatial/spatialDigest.js': 'owner-deferred — feeds seaLanes/teleportEdges (owner PORT/TELEPORT rules; siege=node-starvation not edge-severance)'` (the surrounding note at :183 names buildSeaLanes/buildTeleportEdges and "the owner's PORT §4j / [TELEPORT]" rules).
ownerQuestions.blocks: Any LG wave that changes who is in the bloc — the alliance/trade passage predicate, the wartime preemption rule, and any confiscation or lockdown arm that has to know whether a besieged or ruined holder is still on the network.
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Keep the deferral as it stands while the LG volume is written — the current answer (siege starves the node, it never severs the edge) is the one the built code already implements and the one §46a's node-starvation paragraph endorses; ask the owner only at the wave that first makes bloc membership pay a cost (the toll / preemption car), not before.

ownerQuestions.question: Whether a settlement too poor to fund a fleet still fields a token squadron, or fields none at all — the standing vetoable floor on the vessel family's strength derivation.
ownerQuestions.source: src/domain/spatial/navalLayer.js:69-71 — `[JUDGMENT, vetoable: AFFORD_MIN > 0 — a standing shipyard always fields at least a token squadron; poverty rents the fleet DOWN (the mercenary "reinforces little" idiom), it does not evaporate a yard that exists. Say "veto" to drop the floor (subsistence ⇒ no navy).]` with `AFFORD_MIN: 0.15` at :73.
ownerQuestions.blocks: The fleet-count derivation §46a item 2 asks for, which must read the same tier/prosperity substrate — a poverty floor of zero would mean a poor port has no vessels to allocate at all, which changes the pool's dormancy behaviour rather than just its numbers.
ownerQuestions.recommendation: Leave the floor in place and carry the same shape into the fleet count when it is built (one derivation family for count, strength and rebuild speed, per the §46a addendum) — flag it to the owner as a single question at the pool car rather than twice.

THE FLAG-MINT SEVENTH-PATH LAW — ODQ §49.3 (standing, all volumes): "every packet that mints an engine-gated flag INCLUDES `tests/domain/subsystemRowsVirtual.test.js` in its manifest and prices its three literal edits". Both LG flags are engine-gated, so both cars carry that manifest entry. The file exists at the slot (tests/domain/subsystemRowsVirtual.test.js, 62 KB), and the ordered-equality pin §49.1 names is live in it.

THE CORE GRAPH BEFORE THE LATE WAVES — ODQ §46b closing: "All three are LATE LG waves (consumers of the core graph/pool), producers-before-prose binding as ever"; §46c closing: "An ES×LG×POP seam, late-wave, producers first"; §125.6: "the affected waves re-price at their compiles (LG-0/1 the predicate, LG-5 the replenishment, LG-8/9+ the news chain and captivity, WY/POP-adjacent the speed law)". The circle half of that core graph IS landed (teleportEdges.js), so the predicate car (LG-0/1) starts from a real graph rather than from nothing; the airship half is not, so every air member sits behind one unbuilt mode.

4. CODE-SIDE ORDERING THE RECORD DOES NOT NAME, found at the slot:
   • The airship edge set must land in the ALREADY-RESERVED `airField` slot without moving key order — src/domain/spatial/spatialDigest.js:186 "The KEY ORDER is fixed (airField, seaLanes, seasonalOverlay, teleportEdges) so a [digest stays byte-stable]", :193 the literal `{ airField: null, … }`. Six tests pin it null (listed in the airship row), so lighting it is a declared golden movement, not a silent one.
   • Any new frozen edge set only appears on a RE-CANONIZE — teleportEdges.js:61-64 "Bumping it is a DISCRETE re-canonize event (§V.1) — an existing frozen digest keeps its own teleportEdges forever". Existing worlds gain airships only at a receipted re-canonize, which is the same seam §46's "dormancy byte-identity" disposition relies on.
   • The pool must be built on the sea substrate that already exists, or it will fork the truth: W-NAVY (navalLayer.js + navalKernel.js, behind `navalEnabled`, LIT at simulationRules.js:646) already owns convoys, lane capacity and sea battles. §46a item 6's "THE WHOLE MODEL GENERALIZES TO SEA" therefore reads at the slot as a REFIT of W-NAVY, not a new build beside it.
   • The rebuild timer must use the chair's named spelling `cooldownUntil` (§46a addendum), whose only landed instances are npcLadderChallenge.js:258 and demographicsPlans.js:120 — a vessel timer is the third instance, not the first.

5. STILL UNANSWERED AND NOT VISIBLE IN CODE — the wartime preemption question the brief calls out: ODQ §125.1 item 1 "in WARTIME military/envoy use PREEMPTS trade use of limited capacity — ⚠ the second is ASKED of the owner below rather than assumed", chair-ruled vetoably at §125a "TRADE PASSAGE IS PREEMPTED ENTIRELY — traders revert to roads for the duration … Say 'veto' with 'priority' or 'reserve' to flip." Nothing in code touches it, and nothing can until the circle edge acquires a throttle it does not have (teleportEdges.js:42-44).
result.sizes:
THE RECORD GIVES NO CAR COUNT for #33 — the brief sizes it only as "XL" and names it "the biggest unbuilt block"'s sibling, "a new capability rather than a completion". §125.6 names the wave slots (LG-0/1, LG-5, LG-8/9+) without pricing them, and §46's chair disposition defers the volume to "the next architecture sitting", which never sat.

MY OWN ESTIMATE of the unbuilt remainder, read off what is and is not at the slot — an estimate, not a measured price, and deliberately generous on the members with a landed substrate to compose against:

• Circle passage predicate + alliance/trade widening + toll booking + the §125a wartime preemption (needs a capacity throttle the edge does not yet have) — ~3 cars
• Airships as a mode: the airField edge set builder, the routing read, the origin-port-only rule, the reduced-time factor, the air battle on the sea-battle machinery — ~4 cars
• The unified vessel pool: fleet-count derivation, trade-or-war allocation, dispatched-until-returned unavailability, and the W-NAVY refit that makes sea and air one machinery — ~4 cars
• Rebuild timers on the economic/tier derivation (`cooldownUntil`, third instance) — ~1 car
• Cargo asymmetry, the one-way law, and the retreat-rescue exception with its route-absence query — ~2 cars
• News carriage: the airship carrier plus the §125.3 caravan-to-caravan chain with its continue-or-turn-back decision — ~2 cars
• Envoy vessels across all three modalities, composing the landed road-bound envoy family — ~2 cars
• The infiltration entry-route spectrum: network channel (reachability gate + knowledge predicate), caravan cover with the two scale factors, the individual suspicion/rumour refusal, the wartime gate relaxation — ~4 cars (one less than it would have been: the group-reception half is now landed, see dependencies item 1)
• Confiscation: the army-on-route encounter, the observed-cargo/believed-destination split, the army-supply replenishment, the turn-back reroute, the covered spy's fate coupling — ~3 cars
• Siege lockdown exit modes + capture resolution by captor relation (grading the parked NPC-ransom substrate first, per §46c's fourth addendum chair note) — ~2 cars
• Roaming captivity without ransom, including the bandit-class producer §125.5 warns may be owed — ~2 cars
• Size-scaled speed for armies and migrating columns (§125.4) — ~1 car
• Constitution: the two flags with the §49.3 manifest edits, the persisted-shape widening on the veto surface, registers/ratchet/gate — ~2 cars

ESTIMATED TOTAL: ~32 cars, call it a 28–36 band. Two things pull it DOWN from a cold-start XL: the circle network is already built, mounted and tested (so LG-0's graph car is spent), and the sea vessel layer exists to refit rather than invent. One thing pushes it UP: airships have literally no substrate — a permanently-null reserved slot and a regex over institution names is all that is there.

WHAT THE RECORD GIVES: the brief prices item #32 as a single "XL" and gives a wave count (113, of which "eleven have landed whole and two are part-built, leaving about a hundred and two") but NO car figure anywhere — not in the brief's §32, not in the compiled volume's §5, not in the per-volume wave blocks. The only car-grained numbers the record does give are structural rather than sized: §5's "109 waves", §3's "63 new virtual flags", §4's "14 new sub-ledgers priced", §9's "112 seams pinned".

MY OWN ESTIMATE (stated as an estimate, derived from the landed waves' measured slice counts at the slot, not from the record):

Basis — the 32 built waves show a stable slices-per-wave shape: CW-0w landed as FOUR slices (the couplingRegistryWar.js split, the inclusion ratchet, schema v3 + the desk walker, the proseNumericsWalk fifth detector); IN-0 as FOUR (0a/0b/0c/0d, each its own module); WC-0 as at least FIVE (WC-0A the stance axes through WC-0E the gate, across peopleLedger/warStance/lawBandModulation/contributionLedger); ES-5 as FOUR after the a/b/c/d split; EP-3 as TWO slices but sixteen re-root sites (RS-1..RS-16); HB-2 as ONE. The mean is roughly 2.5 cars, with a long tail at the conservation-walker and convergence waves.

- The 80 UNBUILT waves at ~2.5 cars each → ~200 cars. The distribution is not flat: WC's 16 unbuilt waves and WY's 12 are the heaviest (WC carries a conservation walker, two ledger mints and a round-trip pin; WY's five SURFACE waves are UI work stacked on engine work), while POP's 8 and INT's 8 sit nearer 2 cars apiece.
- The 5 PART-BUILT remainders (GR-4's later succession slices, GR-5's five remaining conjuncts — simulationRules.js:413 says "GR-5 as chartered is six", TR-9's eight pending→real row conversions, WF-8's four further narration members plus its unminted flag, ES-6's narrowed-away remainder) → ~10-14 cars.
- The six convergence waves that close families (GR-7, IN-6, WF-9, POP-7, HB-9, CW-3) are instrument-heavy and I price each at 3-4 cars rather than 2.5.

TOTAL ESTIMATE: ~200-220 cars for the unbuilt remainder, plus ~12 for the part-built remainders — call it 210-230 cars. That is an estimate from measured slice shape at the slot; it is not a figure the record supplies and must not be cited as one.

SIZE CORRECTION WORTH RECORDING: the record's "about a hundred and two [remaining]" is too pessimistic by roughly twenty waves. The code shows 80 unbuilt, not 102 — so any car pricing ever derived from the 102 figure is ~20% high.

result.summary:
THE RECORD IS WRONG ABOUT FIVE OF THE SEVEN PROGRAMMES, and this is a third "the record corrected by the code" after §928 and §930. The brief calls these "designed programmes [that] stand sealed and unbuilt". At the build slot (claude/composite-r4 @ f73bdbf16) six of the seven are substantially or wholly BUILT, most of them built-and-dark behind virtual flags, with full test batteries and certification rows.

A treasury layer EXISTS: src/domain/worldPulse/treasury.js (1,302 lines, 33 exports), wired into the pulse kernel, with taxation, an upkeep sink, a conserved coin-flow ledger, two news beats, a band chip on the dossier glance and a coffers read feeding both war pressure surfaces. Cars 1a/1b/2/3 landed; only car 4 is unbuilt. The brief's "blocked on two questions you have not answered" is stale — treasury.js:10-13 names those two questions as ANSWERED (Q10/A1.21 and Q11/A1.23, ODQ §763.2) and the founding ruling as REVERSED by owner order (§731.1, Q-W8 GRANTED).

A political layer EXISTS: W-SEAT D1-D10 across eleven src modules with three certification rows and three minted virtual flags. Cars SEAT-1, 2a, 2b, 2c, 3, 4, 5, 7a/78 landed. Only SEAT-8 (D11's intervention market + the `civilContests` ledger) is unbuilt, and it is owner-gated in code as a new persisted shape.

The season cap that "locks out the whole world instead of one person" is CURED at the slot and pinned by the convicting two-subject test. The brief lists it as live work.

W-DESK landed as DESK-1 through DESK-5. The two operations cars are the two WIRING cars — W-OPS O1-O5, O6-B and O7 all shipped as dark leaves (3,809 lines across seven modules). The WEAVE shows ~17 of its ~21 cars landed.

W-ARMS IS THE ONE THING GENUINELY UNBUILT. Zero hits for W-ARMS, heraldryEnabled, armsEnabled, blazonEnabled, generateArms, deriveArms, houseArms, factionArms, settlementArms, blazon, coatOfArms across src, tests and supabase. The only emblem generator in the tree is the vendored FMG fork's own, inside a minified bundle, guarded solely by a licence walker.

   · W-SEAT SEAT-8 → the `civilContests` persisted shape, owner-gated per subsystemRowsSeat.js:162. Nothing else blocks the last political car.

result.summary:
I opened every path:line the code reader cited and re-searched the UNBUILT rows with the record's own module names plus my own spellings. The BUILT and PART-BUILT rows survive — the teleport bloc is real, mounted, opted-in live and covered by 449 lines of tests — but both readers are wrong in the same direction, and the code wins for the third time this week.

THE THREE VERDICT CHANGES. (1) AIRSHIPS are PART-BUILT, not UNBUILT. The code reader dismissed all 49 hits as "an INSTITUTION NAME STRING or prose"; in fact there is a landed, pulse-mounted, three-file-tested airship LOGISTICS channel — FOOD_IMPORT_RATES (foodImportRates.js:17-22) prices an open-sky airship at 0.30 and a blockade-running one at 0.15, foodGenerator.js:140-146/:446 emits the channel verdict, four modules consume it, and blockadeTransport.js stamps the dock's impairment inside the live pulse at pulseKernel.js:578. What is missing is §46 item 2's travel mode: airField is hard-null with eight assertions pinning it, and there is no air route, no reduced-time factor and no air battle. (2) CARGO ASYMMETRY is PART-BUILT: navalKernel.js:330-353's `seaLiftDelivered` stamp plus the total absence of a homeward convoy path means troops already flow toward war by sea and never back — the outcome is enforced, the law is not, which is a trap, because the first LG car that adds a trade return leg would silently repeal it. (3) The record reader's headline "nothing in it has landed" is refuted: the circle network, the airship import channel, the ship and teleport news carriers, a persisted capture-and-custody ledger with a `caught_spying` cause, and the group-reception machinery §49 declared absent are all at the slot.

THE BIGGEST MISS ON BOTH SIDES is src/domain/worldPulse/foreignGuestHold.js — a persisted spatialLedgers family (`foreignGuestHolds`, schemaVersion 1, closed cause and close-reason vocabularies, the interrupted journey preserved for resumption) that the siege-lockdown, capture-resolution and roaming-captivity rows all depend on and neither reader found. Reading it answers the record reader's owner question 4 far more cheaply than it was posed: NPC ransom is not parked — ransomClaim.js mints it and envoyRansomStage.js sequences it — and the code names its own two blockers, one an owner gate and one not. envoyRansomStage.js:39-42: "NOTHING IS PERSISTED HERE, AND THAT IS AN OWNER GATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT." infiltrationDrift.js's parked 'ransom' exit: "A ransom can be minted and cannot be concluded" because "release is a frozen member of FOREIGN_GUEST_HOLD_CLOSE_REASONS with ZERO writers in src/", unblocked by "a pulse-side close with reason release, which is a writer and not a schema change: the one park here with a dated road rather than a ruling." The owner is owed one persistence ruling, not an unparking of the WR-era seat-ransom family.

OWNER-GATE QUOTES: all five verified verbatim in the ledger ODQ at a803dee7a — §46 (~1771-1773), §48 ruling 4 (~1985), §46c fourth addendum chair note (~1889-1903), §125.1 (~4628-4633), §125a (~4669-4684). On the brief's disputed sentence, both readers are half right: §125.1 does put the wartime question to the owner and §125a does rule it, but only "chair under 'i trust your judgement' … vetoable", so the owner never answered. The brief should be amended, not struck.

COUNTS CORRECTED: FLAG_DEFAULTS is 38 keys, not 30 (none LG); airField carries eight null assertions across six files plus a key-order pin, not six tests; navalEnabled appears in four preset light-lists including the default; and — the one that would cost a compile — the record's §148.2 fourth flag-mint obligation names "two exact literal 22s" in contributionLedgerShape.test.js, which now reads "holds the triple bijection at 28" with its own raise log at :51-60. An LG-0 packet compiled against the record edits the wrong literal.

result.summary:
The brief's sentence for #34 — "several designed programmes stand sealed and unbuilt" — is false for six of its seven members, and this is the third "the record corrected by the code" after §928 and §930. Of 73 named build units I count 45 BUILT, 11 PART-BUILT and 17 UNBUILT; W-ARMS is the only member where the brief is exactly right, and I confirmed that with sixteen distinct search terms rather than the code reader's ten.

The code reader is broadly right and the record reader is broadly stale, but both are wrong in ways that matter, and I refuted rows on each side.

Against the CODE READER. Its W-OPS row is the biggest overstatement: it calls seven leaves BUILT when six of the seven have ZERO src importers and the seventh (operationGrammar) is imported only by missionDispatcher, which nothing imports — the certification rows say so themselves ("WHAT THE FLAG LIGHTS, EXACTLY ONE THING AT THIS CAR: nothing", subsystemRowsOps.js:193). That is PART-BUILT, not BUILT, and the line count is 4,009 not 3,809. Its WEAVE row is the biggest understatement: it counted "~17 of ~21" while omitting the entire POLIS family and inventing NET-1b and NET-1c, which return zero hits; my census finds 22 of ~28 with code. Its ENC-5 row is wrong in identity — ENC-5's WORDS landed and are transcribed at envoyChanceMeetingReceiptPools.js under a preserve seal; only the grudge fold is owed, so PART-BUILT. Its SEAT-6 UNKNOWN is avoidable: the record settles it at §870.4 as "deferred priced", so UNBUILT. And its DESK collision warning missed that DESK-4 itself collides with a prose-desk car at warFaithStateProse.js:2.

Against the RECORD READER. Five WEAVE cars it lists as unbuilt are built at the slot and the code wins: NET-2 (routeNetworkGenesis.js:63), POLIS-3 (TravelRingsLayer.jsx, mounted at MapOverlay.jsx:354), POLIS-4 (TerritoryLayer.jsx, mounted at :332), VAR-3 (InstantWorldEntry.jsx:56/:94/:267) and SEAM-5 (LivingWorldGates.jsx). Its W-DESK row is the sharpest miss: it correctly reports that W-DESK appears exactly twice in the 32,673-line ODQ and was never dispatched — and all five cars are nevertheless in the tree, named car-for-car against §730.3's own wording, and mounted through WorldMapStage → MapOverlay and WorldMap → RealmInspector → HeraldBody. The record simply never learned that this wave was built.

Two rows NEITHER reader carried, both unbuilt: ENC-7 (zero hits; the seven `eliteBleed` hits are the unrelated DEEP COUPLINGS D-7f family — a trap for anyone greping the description rather than the car name), and the TE-CEIL-blocked SEAT-2a §H arm plus SEAT-4's chooser (`TE-CEIL` returns zero hits in src, so no cure landed).

On the owner gates: I opened every §-anchor the record reader cited in docs/OWNER_DECISION_QUEUE.md on the ledger branch and every quotation is verbatim — §730.4's Q-W8 row, §731.1's grant ("do Q-W8 regardless…"), §737.1's dispatch bar, §746.2's veto sentence, §820's full Q-S3 ruling with its cost sentence, §729.4's seven-plus-one batch, §882.10's rows 4 and 9, §879.11 R2's one-word veto, §728.1's ratification. The code reader's four certification-row quotes are verbatim too. No misquotation on either side.

The single most actionable finding is the code reader's, and it is not a build item: simulationRules.js:393-398 holds `treasuryEnabled` dark until W-COIN-2's band chip lands, that chip landed at dossierViewModel.js:409 `deriveTreasuryGlance`, and the key is still in no preset. A fully built, fully wired, fully tested treasury layer is invisible on every world anyone plays, and lighting it moves same-seed output on three presets — so it is an owner decision that the interim law's own condition has already unblocked.
